content: Bitwarden's own 'Data Privacy for Website Icons' docs acknowledge their icon service sends the domain of every saved login to Bitwarden's icon servers (or self-hosted equivalent) to fetch favicons, and documents a client setting to disable this for privacy. Vaultwarden supports configurable ICON_SERVICE (internal/bitwarden/duckduckgo/google/custom-template) and an explicit disable-icon-download option; its unauthenticated public /icons endpoint has an open community-flagged privacy issue (GitHub discussion #2115) allowing enumeration of which domains an instance has cached, i.e. even the self-hosted 'internal' fetch mode leaks domain-fetch timing/caching behavior if the endpoint is public. For a zero-knowledge-postured instance, the safe default is no automatic third-party favicon fetching at all in this phase -- render the neutral type-icon (Vault/CreditCard/etc., already part of the row per UI-SPEC) as the sole visual, deferring any favicon fetch (self-hosted proxy or client-direct with explicit opt-in) to a later phase.
